title: Testing Excel header output: read back with header=None because read_excel forward-fills empty MultiIndex header cells
answers: how to test to_excel MultiIndex column headers
why does my to_excel round-trip test pass even though the header is wrong
read_excel header=[0,1] fills blank header cells
body:
`pd.read_excel(path, header=[0, 1])` forward-fills empty header cells. A round-trip test can therefore hide a wrong or blank header cell: an earlier test for GH#62340 passed on main even though the bug was still there.
To check the exact cells written, read the raw rows with `pd.read_excel(tmp_excel, header=None, nrows=<n header rows>)`. Compare the result to a plain DataFrame in which the blank cells are np.nan.
See pandas/tests/io/excel/test_writers.py:TestExcelWriter.test_to_excel_multiindex_nan_column_label. It uses the `merge_cells` and `tmp_excel` fixtures, so it runs for every engine and every merge_cells setting.
applies: tests for DataFrame.to_excel header/index formatting in pandas/tests/io/excel
